title: Construct String With Repeat Limit
summary: Given a string s and an integer repeatLimit , construct the lexicographically largest string possible such that no character appears more than repeatLimit times consecutively.
statement: Given a string s and an integer repeatLimit , construct the lexicographically largest string possible such that no character appears more than repeatLimit times consecutively. Use the characters from s without needing to use all of them.
constraints: Use each available lowercase character at most as many times as it occurs; unused characters are allowed.
No character may occur more than repeat_limit times consecutively.
Return the lexicographically largest valid string.
reference_solution:
def largest_repeat_limited_string(s,repeat_limit):
    from collections import Counter
    counts=Counter(s);answer=[]
    while counts:
        largest=max(counts);take=min(counts[largest],repeat_limit)
        answer.append(largest*take);counts[largest]-=take
        if counts[largest]==0:del counts[largest];continue
        smaller=[char for char in counts if char<largest]
        if not smaller:break
        breaker=max(smaller);answer.append(breaker);counts[breaker]-=1
        if counts[breaker]==0:del counts[breaker]
    return ''.join(answer)

hints: Always prefer the largest character that can legally extend the answer.
Take up to repeat_limit copies of the largest remaining character; if copies remain, insert the largest smaller breaker.
Maintain character counts, repeatedly append the largest run, then one best breaker when required.
Any smaller choice while a larger legal character exists makes the string lexicographically worse; the largest breaker preserves the best possible next position.

tests.explanation: Use the two z characters first, then three c characters, a as a breaker, and the final c: zzcccac.
The lexicographically largest construction is bbabaa.
